$comment: Rad Dog / Neon Surf art data. Lengths are in units of a 400 x 400 artboard (multiply by artboard short side / 400), or given as percentages. Colours are roles only; hex values always come from the product's Wada combination. Values marked 'rule of thumb' are our reading of 1980s-90s surf and skate graphics, not measured from a corpus.

line.$comment: The outline: a fat, even black line around every drawn shape, like a technical pen or brush outline on a screen-printed deck.
line.continuity: Every shape is closed and outlined. Shapes that touch share one fused outline (draw all ink outlines first, then all fills on top).
line.terminals: Round ends on open strokes (tails, motion lines, squiggles).
rules: One outline weight per piece for silhouettes; interior details (mouth, fur, wave lines) at about 60% of it.
Outlines are always ink (Wada Black). Never coloured, grey or dashed.
No sketchy, broken or hairline strokes: the line should look inked and confident.
Line weight is fixed per artboard: do not scale strokes with the objects.

shape.$comment: Cartoon shapes: chunky, rounded, closed, readable as silhouettes.

character.$comment: Proportions for mascots and characters. Rule of thumb from 1980s surfwear mascots.
character.headShare: The head is 40-50% of the character's total height.
character.eyes: Big eyes or, as the signature, solid black shades with one white glint stroke.
character.limbs: Rounded ellipses or tubes with no elbows or knees drawn; paws and hands as mittens with 3-4 fingers.
character.pose: Leaning into the diagonal of the piece (10-20 degrees), mid-action: riding, skating, jumping, falling off.
character.expression: One clear feeling: cool, stoked or wiped out. Tongue out, grin or open mouth.

blob.smoothing: Closed Catmull-Rom curve through the points (tension 0.5).

shape.points: Points are allowed on Memphis confetti (triangles, zigzags), starbursts and splatter drips; everything that is a character or object is rounded.
rules: Every object is a closed, outlined shape with a flat fill.
The character's fill is paper (Wada White) or the combination's lightest colour, so it pops from the ground.
No realistic anatomy, no rendered volume; a single flat highlight stroke is the only modelling.

corners.$comment: Rounded, chunky corners for layout and UI around the art. Pixels at 1x for screens.

use.button: pill, with ink outline and a hard ink block shadow
use.chip / sticker: pill or lg, rotated -6 to 6 degrees
use.card: lg, ink outline, hard block shadow
use.image: lg with an ink outline, or a die-cut sticker shape with a fat white border

corners.nested: An inner radius is the outer radius minus the padding between them.
corners.print: On posters, sticker corners are 25-50% of the sticker's short side.

blockShadow.$comment: The hard, offset ink shadow used on type, stickers and UI. It is a flat second shape, not a blurred shadow.
blockShadow.use: Headline lettering, stickers, buttons, cards. Not on the illustration itself (the outline already separates it).

diagonals.$comment: Angles in degrees, negative = rising left to right. Rule of thumb.
diagonals.rule: Pick one dominant direction (usually rising left to right) and keep the headline, pattern band and the character's motion on it. Stickers may counter-rotate by a few degrees for life.

composition.grid: 6 columns on posters, 12 on screen. Text stacks in the top 40%, the hero anchors to the bottom edge or bleeds off one edge.

placements.use: Hero riding on a wave or band across the bottom half; headline stacked top-left on the tilt (the sample poster).
Hero inside a round or shield badge with the brand on a ribbon; square social posts and merch.
Hero bursting out of a frame (a board, a TV, a sun) and breaking its outline; for launches.
Checkerboard or sunset stripes as a full background with one big sticker headline; for banners and thumbnails where there is no room for a character.

composition.pairing: Picture and headline are a pair: the character acts out the benefit, the headline says the specific fact.
rules: One focal point: the hero. Pattern sits behind it or around the edges.
Keep text off the busiest pattern; put it on calm ground or a sticker.
The brand sticker sits within one sticker-height of the headline.

pattern.$comment: The pattern vocabulary. Use at most two per piece (composition.maxElements.patterns).

checkerboard.use: A band on the dominant diagonal, a floor, a border.

sunsetStripes.thicknessGrowth: Stripes start at about 1% of the sun's diameter and grow by about 1% each, lower stripes thicker.
sunsetStripes.use: Cuts in the lower half of a sun disc, in the ground colour.

memphisConfetti.use: Scattered in empty corners, never touching the headline.

splatter.use: Paint flicks in accent or support colours near the hero or in a corner.

sprayStipple.falloff: Dense at the edge of the shape, fading out over 10% of the artboard.
sprayStipple.use: Airbrush glow done with dots, around a sun or behind a character. Prints in one ink.

waveCurl.use: The signature landscape: a curling wave with scalloped white foam.

palm.use: Silhouette in ink at the frame edge, cropped. Optional; skip it when the piece already has two patterns.

sticker.$comment: Badges and stickers for brand, labels, prices and calls to action.
rules: Stickers carry the brand, a price, a date or a CTA. Never a paragraph.
A die-cut white border plus ink outline for photos and characters used as stickers.
At most three stickers per piece.

palette.$comment: Share of the visible area for each colour role. Colours come from the product's Wada combination; this style uses every colour of the combination, not just bg and accent.

sea.from: combination support or ink colour (the coolest colour)

ink.use: Every outline, checkerboard, block shadows, text ribbons.

accent.use: One or two hot details: the board, the sun, the tongue, a splatter.

method: Start from the bright set in recommendedCombinations.
The ground is the lightest saturated colour (yellow, lemon, grenadine pink, orange yellow); text on it is ink.
The sea is the coolest colour (teal, sea green, peacock, cerulean, blue).
If the combination has only two colours, add black and white only; do not borrow a third colour.
Check text contrast: headline in paper with an ink outline always passes; body text is ink on the ground or paper on an ink ribbon.
Dark mode: ink ground, the combination's colours on characters and type, paper for outlines only on small UI.

airbrush.allowed: One linear fade per piece, on the sun or sky only, between two colours of the same combination; or spray stipple instead (prints in one ink).
airbrush.never: Fades on type, glows, blurred shadows, rainbow gradients.

recommendedCombinations.why: The flagship: Wada's purest yellow ground, a coral sun and a surf-blue sea. AA for black text (15.9:1).
The classic 1980s hot pink and teal pair, close to fluorescent pink on turquoise. Black text 7.2:1.
Yellow and black sticker energy with a carmine hot spot; black is already in the combination.
The stripped-down version: yellow ground, black outline and checkerboard. Best for stickers and small formats.
Primary pop for skate-deck energy: red board, yellow ground, blue sea.
Pink ground with black graphics: the loudest two-colour print, cheap to screen-print.
Sunset magenta and orange on black: the dusk and night-session variant.
Hot orange-red and teal with grey; works in dark mode on a black ground.
Pink, gold and purple: the sunset sky combination, softer for lifestyle products.
Lemon ground with a tropical aqua: the sunniest, friendliest option.
Orange-yellow ground with peacock sea; a warmer, slightly vintage 1970s-into-80s surf look.

palette.avoid: Combinations whose brightest colour is a muted, olive or dark yellow (they read dirty at this saturation), and pastel-only combinations (they lose the energy).

extensions.what: Real fluorescent colour. No Wada colour (and no CMYK or sRGB colour) is fluorescent; neon surfwear used fluorescent pigments and Day-Glo-type spot inks.
extensions.print: Pantone fluorescent spot inks from the 801-807 basic range (801 blue, 802 green, 803 yellow, 804 orange, 805 red, 806 pink, 807 magenta-violet; check names against a physical Pantone swatch book, sources disagree), or a printer with fluorescent pink and yellow channels. Use at most two fluorescent spots per piece, replacing the combination's hottest colours (ground and accent). Keep outlines in a standard black.
extensions.screen: Screens cannot show fluorescence. On screen, map the fluorescent roles to the most saturated sRGB colours a product chooses (e.g. a 'screen neon' set for pink, green, yellow and cyan) and use them only for small highlights; the hex values would need adding to the product's palette and approving.
caveats: Fluorescent inks fade in sunlight faster than process inks; not for long-life outdoor signage.
Proof physically: on-screen and PDF previews of fluorescent spots are simulations.
Fluorescent pink substituted for magenta cannot make deep reds; keep reds as standard inks.

rules: One combination per piece; use all of its colours, plus ink and paper.
No blurred shadows or glows; the only shadow is the hard block shadow.
Text colour on the ground uses ink, or paper with an ink outline.

sprayStipple.use: Airbrush effect around suns, characters and splats.

halftone.use: Comic-book shading on a sky or wave face, in ink or the sea colour.

texture.grain: Optional screen-print grain or slight misregistration (0.5-1% offset of the fill against the outline) on print and merch; never on UI.

vocabulary.$comment: Symbols and what they usually say. Combine one from the product's world with one from the benefit, then hand it to the hero.

means: the end of a good day

symbols.note: Hawaiian gesture; use it as greeting, not as a costume.

avoid.why: Sacred and cultural forms from Polynesian peoples used as decoration; caricature and appropriation (research.md 5).
A tourist caricature of Native Hawaiian culture, often sexualised.
1980s surf advertising cliché; objectifying and off-message.

avoid.symbol: Screaming Hand, Rude Dog or other existing mascots
avoid.why: Trademarked characters; reference the attitude, never the character.
Belongs to the neighbouring 'neon ooze' and skate-horror look; off-brand for most products.
Reads as pastiche; the wit should be visual.

method.$comment: How to find the one image: give the benefit to a character and make it a sight gag.
recipe: Write the one message in a sentence (W1).
Pick the hero: the product's mascot, or an animal or object from the product's world that can wear shades.
Pick the action from the benefit (riding, catching, skating, jumping, falling and getting up).
Add one sight gag that makes it specific (the dog rides a croissant instead of a board; the wave is made of coffee).
Choose one setting device (wave, sun, checker band) and at most one more pattern.
Test: readable in 2 seconds without words? Would a competitor's ad use it? Is the joke on the situation, never on a culture or a person?

examples.action: wearing shades and setting into the sea

checklist: One hero at 30-45% of the area; readable in 2 seconds without words.
Every shape outlined in ink at one weight (1.5% of the short side); type with outline and block shadow.
One dominant diagonal; at most two angles.
At most two patterns; at least 25% calm ground.
One Wada combination from the bright set, plus ink and paper; at most one airbrush fade.
Brand sticker next to the headline; text on calm ground or a sticker.
No faux-Polynesian motifs, no existing mascots, no fake slang.
